title: Halcyon Grid identity rebuild: prep-and-vectorize an AI-generated logo export into a clean multi-format mark, author a deeper merch colourway from primitives, neutralize six mixed-light brand-in-use photos to one white point, and data-merge a press-ready brand sheet
grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Upwork brief (the client had a logo 'created on AI' and needed it turned into a 'vector file so it can be used in multiple platforms' with the logo 'high-quality across different formats'). Laundered to a fictional SaaS startup, 'Halcyon Grid' — no real company, product, trademark, or software is named anywhere in the task-facing fields (the AI generators named under inputs[].gen_model are pipeline metadata, left as-is per the IP rule). REASONABLY ENRICHED into a runnable long-horizon Adobe-connector benchmark and repaired against the ground-truth boundary: (1) the from-scratch vector comes ONLY from the raster tracer applied to the client's supplied AI export — an honest raster->SVG path, never authored art; (2) the transparency is produced by knocking the outer off-white card, NOT by the banned select->invert->solid-fill chain; (3) the one-colour mark is produced by feeding the mark SELECTION to the tracer (which returns a single-colour silhouette), NOT by a whole-image colour overlay that cannot knock cleanly; (4) the deeper merch colourway is a masked, luminosity-preserving within-family recolour (the only masked recolour path), not a flat fill or whole-image tint; (5) the designed endpoint is a genuine authored page-layout template data-merged one-record-per-page so type is actually SET, replacing the original's typeset-punt to a bare hand-off folder; (6) the deprecated brightness/contrast tool is replaced by the primitive-adjustments tool. The mark is deliberately an OPEN three-stroke wind/data-flow glyph (no enclosed negative space) so the knockout and one-colour silhouette are clean without any dark-ground counter-punch. To make cross-asset consistency a trippable target, the client is modelled as also supplying six photographs of the brand already in use, each carrying an in-frame 18% grey card and shot under mismatched light — with one shot (an etched reception sign) that looks like clean logo art but is a photograph and must never reach the tracer.
one_line_ask: Turn Halcyon Grid's flat AI logo export into a clean, infinitely scalable full-colour vector by straightening, cleaning and knocking it to transparency before tracing; derive a single-colour silhouette mark, an agent-authored deeper merch colourway via masked recolour, a halftone print treatment, and platform-sized raster exports; neutralize six mixed-light brand-in-use photos to the grey card each one carries so they read as one set; recommend a matching font pairing; and data-merge the client's authored page-layout template into one press-ready brand sheet, one page per item.
full_brief: Halcyon Grid is an analytics startup that generated its logo with an AI image tool and only has the flat square export the tool produced — a teal-and-charcoal mark (an open three-stroke wind/data-flow glyph beside the wordmark) sitting on a faint off-white textured card, with the soft edges, faint noise and a baseline that tips a couple of degrees off level that those tools leave behind. That single raster is unusable across the places the brand now lives: it does not scale, has no transparency, and looks nothing like the crisp identity we need on our site, app icon, deck, sign vinyl and one-colour merch. Separately, we are sending a folder of photographs of the brand already out in the world — our tote, an embroidered cap, a ceramic mug, a laptop sticker, a pull-up banner and our etched reception sign — each shot on a different day under whatever light happened to be there, so straight out of the folder they look like a mismatched jumble; we dropped a small grey reference card into the corner of every one so you can bring them to a single, consistent look. What we need back: (1) a clean, infinitely scalable full-colour vector of the mark, cleaned of the AI export's tilt, noise and textured ground BEFORE it is traced so the paths are crisp; (2) a single-colour version of the mark for vinyl, embroidery and small favicons; (3) a distinct on-brand merch colourway — a deeper, richer take on our teal that still reads as us, applied only to the mark's own colour so its shapes and edges are untouched; (4) a print-screen / halftone treatment of the mark for posters and apparel; (5) platform-sized raster exports of the mark — a 1024 app icon, a 512 social avatar and a wide site-header bug — each crisp at its target size and honestly reframed from the cleaned mark, never enlarged past it; (6) a recommended font pairing that matches the wordmark so we can extend the identity in decks and docs; and (7) the six photographs brought to one consistent, true-to-life look — each neutralised to the grey card it carries so the whole set shares a single white point and reads as one professional series, holding our real product colours true. Finally, assemble everything into a single press-ready brand sheet — one page per logo variant and one page per in-use photograph — with each item's name, its usage rule, its minimum size and its clear-space note set from the field sheet we are providing, the matching artwork placed on its page, and the mark locked into every masthead. Bind our wording verbatim; do not rewrite the usage rules or invent copy. Acceptance: the vectors are clean and scale without artefacts; the raster exports are crisp and never upscaled; every photograph's grey card reads as one shared neutral white point with our product colours intact; and the finished sheet has exactly one page per item we listed.

inputs.name: halcyon_logo_master_raw.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A 2048x2048 PNG of an AI-generated tech-startup logo exactly as it would look straight out of an image generator: a teal (#178C8C) and charcoal (#2B2F33) brand mark for 'Halcyon Grid' — an OPEN icon of three stacked, separated curved wind/data-flow strokes (no closed loops, no enclosed negative space) to the LEFT of the wordmark 'Halcyon Grid' in a modern semibold sans-serif. The logo sits centred on a faint off-white (#F4F2EE) softly textured paper-like card that fills the frame. Render it with the tell-tale traits of an AI raster export: very slightly soft anti-aliased edges, a faint amount of luminance noise across the background, mild uneven lighting, and the whole logo rotated about 2.5 degrees clockwise so the baseline is not level. Crisp, readable text, accurate kerning, no extra glyphs, no watermark, sharp enough that the letterforms are legible. Photographic-flat, not glossy 3D.
inputs.realism_notes: TRACEABLE SOURCE — the ONLY input that may be fed to the raster tracer, and only after prep. Must be a believable AI export, not a pre-cleaned vector: keep the off-white textured card (no transparency), the soft edges, the faint noise, and the ~2.5deg clockwise tilt — these are the exact defects the chain must fix (auto-straighten -> primitive tone/contrast crisp -> crop to bounds -> knock the outer card to transparency) BEFORE tracing; a naive agent that traces the raw file bakes in the tilt, the paper texture and a soft doubled edge, and the failure is only visible in the SVG path data. The icon is deliberately THREE SEPARATED OPEN STROKES with no enclosed counters, so knocking the outer card to transparency and the selection->silhouette one-colour trace are both clean without any dark-ground interior-counter punch (which the connector cannot do). 2048px so the 1024 icon / 512 avatar / wide header exports are pure downscales, never upscales. 8-bit RGB PNG, sRGB.

inputs.name: brand_in_use_photos_x6.zip
inputs.gen_prompt: A set of 6 REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless captures of Halcyon Grid branded items in everyday settings, each ~4000-4200 px on the long edge (full-resolution stills straight off the camera), each with a small photographic 18% grey card laid flat in one corner of the frame as a neutral reference, and each showing real surface texture, clutter and candid documentary light — no studio gloss, no CGI: (1) a canvas TOTE BAG with the teal mark screen-printed on it, on a desk under cool bluish office fluorescents, frame tilted ~4 deg; (2) an EMBROIDERED CAP with the mark stitched on the front, warm window light, level; (3) a glazed ceramic MUG with the mark, mixed light, slightly underexposed, tilted ~3 deg; (4) a LAPTOP LID with a die-cut vinyl STICKER of the mark, cool cast, level; (5) a fabric PULL-UP BANNER with the large mark at a small event, warm tungsten light, slightly overexposed; (6) an ETCHED FROSTED-GLASS RECEPTION SIGN carrying the mark, shot straight-on so it looks deceptively like clean flat logo artwork, cool daylight through glass with faint reflections and the frosted texture visible, level. Every shot has the grey card clearly visible and uncropped.
inputs.realism_notes: CROSS-ASSET GREY-CARD BATCH and the TRIAGE DECOY, in one folder. REAL-CAMERA at ~4000 px long edge (not a ~1024-1536 AI raster) precisely so each context tile fills its brand-sheet frame at ~300 DPI by DOWNSCALE ONLY. Deliberately mismatched per frame — cool fluorescent (1,4), warm window/tungsten (2,5), under- (3) and over-exposed (5) — so a single blanket white-balance recipe cannot match the set; each needs its OWN by-eye correction to the grey card it carries, and only the tilted frames (1,3) need straightening. The agent neutralises each in-frame 18% grey card BY EYE (it never reads a pixel/channel/hex) and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure it dialled per frame. THE DECOY is frame 6, the etched frosted-glass sign: shot straight-on it looks like a second, cleaner copy of the logo artwork and tempts the agent to route it to the tracer — but it is a PHOTOGRAPH of frosted, textured, faintly-reflective glass, and tracing it yields garbage weave/reflection paths. Its only correct treatment is the same as the other five: neutralise to its grey card and crop to a context tile for the brand sheet — NEVER trace it. The single flat AI export is the only traceable source. Delivered as a zip of 6 individually addressable full-resolution JPEGs.

inputs.name: halcyon_brandsheet_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built single-record US Letter (8.5x11) portrait brand-sheet page-layout document (.indd/.idml) — ONE item per page. It carries live data-merge placeholder fields <<item_name>>, <<usage_rule>>, <<min_size>>, <<clear_space>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a main artwork frame bound to @image (the variant or the context tile for that row) and a masthead frame at the top of every page bound to @Mark (the single-colour vectorised mark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the masthead mark reaches every page ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-record grid: the merge emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: The one-record-per-page layout merge REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE PAGE PER ROW — so a single-record brand sheet is the correct connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted template with literal typed text would not bind and is banned as a merge target. TWO image columns (@image, @Mark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's own artwork (a vector variant or a neutralised context tile) via @image AND the shared single-colour vector mark via @Mark — so the chain-produced mark reaches every masthead as a merge bind, never free-form placement.

inputs.name: halcyon_brandsheet_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with columns item_name,usage_rule,min_size,clear_space,@image,@Mark holding 10 rows, one per brand-sheet page. Four LOGO-VARIANT rows (Primary Full-Colour Mark; Single-Colour Mark; Merch Colourway; Halftone Print Treatment) and six BRAND-IN-USE rows (Tote; Embroidered Cap; Ceramic Mug; Laptop Sticker; Event Banner; Reception Sign). Each row carries a short verbatim usage rule (e.g. 'Use the full-colour mark on light backgrounds only; never place on busy imagery'), a minimum reproduction size (e.g. '24 px digital / 12 mm print'), and a clear-space note (e.g. 'Keep clear space equal to the glyph height on all sides'). The @image column names the agent-produced artwork file for that row (the vector variant, the colourway/halftone raster, or that item's neutralised context tile). The @Mark column holds the SAME single-colour vector mark file in EVERY row so the masthead mark binds on every page. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<item_name>>,<<usage_rule>>,<<min_size>>,<<clear_space>> and the two @image-path columns @image and @Mark.
inputs.realism_notes: States GOALS only: rows name the brand-sheet items and carry verbatim usage copy; the @image column references AGENT-PRODUCED output filenames the agent names per its OWN triage and prep — it does NOT encode which INPUT gets which treatment, carries no 'type' column, and does not telegraph the trace-vs-photograph decision. Ten rows means the merge must produce exactly ten pages. @Mark carries the identical single-colour vector mark path in all ten rows, giving the chain-produced mark a connector-doable path onto every masthead via the merge (a two-image-column pattern).

outputs.name: halcyon_mark_fullcolor.svg
outputs.spec: Primary deliverable: transparent full-colour vector trace of the cleaned mark — teal glyph + charcoal wordmark as clean continuous paths, scalable to any size. Traced by the raster tracer from the straightened, tonally-crisped, cropped, knocked-to-transparency master (whole-raster colour trace, no selection). On light usage the wordmark's letter counters read as the white ground; the open three-stroke icon has no enclosed counters.

outputs.name: halcyon_mark_onecolor.svg
outputs.spec: Single-colour silhouette vector of the mark for one-colour print, vinyl, embroidery and small favicons — a solid one-colour silhouette produced by feeding the mark SELECTION to the tracer (which returns a single-colour silhouette), NOT a whole-image colour overlay. The open three-stroke icon keeps its separation as a clean silhouette. Also bound into every brand-sheet masthead via the roster @Mark column.

outputs.name: halcyon_mark_transparent.png
outputs.spec: PNG, transparent background, isolated cleaned mark trimmed to bounds — the outer off-white card knocked to transparency (not a select->invert->fill). The reusable source for the colourway, halftone and platform raster exports.

outputs.name: halcyon_mark_merchcolorway.png
outputs.spec: Agent-AUTHORED deeper merch colourway of the mark: the brand teal deepened to a richer within-family pine/deep-teal via a masked, luminosity-preserving two-pass HSL recolour (a small in-family hue nudge plus a saturation/luminance drop) that rides the mark's own luminosity so its shapes and edges are untouched and the charcoal wordmark is unaffected — no flat dead-fill, no whole-image tint. A within-family deepen-and-mute, not a near-complementary rotation.

outputs.name: halcyon_mark_halftone.png
outputs.spec: Halftone / print-screen treatment of the isolated mark for poster and apparel use.

outputs.name: halcyon_icon_1024.png
outputs.spec: 1024x1024 (1:1) app-icon PNG, transparent ground, crisp at target size; honestly reframed from the cleaned transparent mark by crop/downscale (centred on the mark, edges cropped to the square ratio) from the 2048 master — a pure downscale, never a canvas extension or upscale.

outputs.name: halcyon_avatar_512.png
outputs.spec: 512x512 (1:1) social-avatar PNG, transparent ground, crisp at target size; reframed from the cleaned transparent mark by crop/downscale (centred, square ratio) — pure downscale, no upscale.

outputs.name: halcyon_header_bug.png
outputs.spec: 480x120 (4:1 landscape) site-header 'bug' PNG, transparent ground; honestly reframed from the cleaned transparent mark by crop/downscale to the wide ratio (top/bottom cropped away, centred on the mark) — not a canvas extension, not an upscale.

outputs.name: brand_in_use_tiles_x6
outputs.spec: Six grey-card-neutralised, straightened brand-in-use photos, delivered as the product-framed context tiles (grey card cropped OUT) that bind into the merge, alongside their RETAINED pre-crop neutralised masters (grey card still in frame) which the harness keeps as the neutrality-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, two SEPARATE claims): (a) neutralisation is graded on each RETAINED pre-crop neutralised master — its in-frame 18% grey card reads a clean neutral (per-channel spread near zero) with the whole set matched to one shared white point while product colours stay true; (b) card-exclusion is checked separately on each delivered context tile (grey card fully cropped OUT). The neutrality tolerance is never evaluated on the card-cropped tile. Accompanied by a report of the final temperature/tint/exposure move applied to each frame.

outputs.name: halcyon_font_pairing.json
outputs.spec: Recommended brand-safe font pairing matching the traced wordmark's proportions and weight, from the font recommender, so the client can extend the identity into decks and docs. Recommendation only — no from-scratch letterform design.

outputs.name: Halcyon_BrandSheet_perItem_x10.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly ten press-ready US Letter portrait pages — ONE single-record page per roster row (page-count = row-count = 10) — exported from the one-record-per-page layout merge; each page binds its item_name/usage_rule/min_size/clear_space verbatim from the roster with its matching artwork dropped into the @image frame and the single-colour vector mark dropped into the masthead @Mark frame, both by merge bind (never free-form placement); ~300 DPI. The Primary Full-Colour Mark is simply page 1 of the merged set, not a separately exported file.

outputs.name: Halcyon_Vector_Kit asset folder
outputs.spec: Organised CC asset folder collecting the full hand-off kit — both SVGs, the transparent mark, the merch colourway, the halftone, the three platform PNGs, the font pairing and the brand-sheet PDF — packaged for client hand-off.

connector_workflow.note: Single asset load: bring the AI logo export and the six brand-in-use photos into Creative Cloud storage. The authored template and roster are supplied inputs consumed at the merge. Every later step consumes a named prior output; this is the only ingest.

LOGO BRANCH, prep-before-trace step 1. Level the tilt baked into the AI export so the wordmark baseline is square — tracing the tilted raw file would bake the rotation into the paths. REPORT the correcting angle.

Prep-before-trace step 2 (replaces the deprecated brightness/contrast tool). By eye, push contrast/clarity and even the mild AI lighting so the teal glyph and charcoal wordmark separate hard from the off-white card and the faint noise is crushed — a soft, low-contrast raster traces into ragged doubled edges. Tone/contrast only, no rotation.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop the surrounding card so the canvas hugs the artwork before isolating, so the trace sees only the mark, not surplus paper.

Prep-before-trace step 4 and a named deliverable: knock the outer off-white card to transparency, isolating the mark. This is the sanctioned knockout (remove_background -> transparency), NOT the banned select->invert->solid-fill chain. The open three-stroke icon has no enclosed counters, so nothing interior needs punching (which the connector cannot do).

DELIVERABLE (primary): whole-raster colour-trace the cleaned transparent mark into the full-colour SVG — teal glyph + charcoal wordmark as separate clean paths. No selection: this is the two-colour path.

Select 'the logo mark shapes' on the cleaned transparent mark to isolate the combined mark from the transparent ground — the input for the one-colour cut path. Semantic object selection, not a hue or coordinate region.

DELIVERABLE (one-colour): vectorize the mark SELECTION, which returns a single-colour silhouette for vinyl, embroidery and small favicons. Same cleaned raster as step 6, deliberately a DIFFERENT tracer use (selection->silhouette vs whole-raster colour trace). Swap the two polarities and the full-colour art loses its colour or the one-colour arrives as unusable two-colour art. Also feeds every masthead via @Mark.
Select 'the teal wind glyph' only (not the charcoal wordmark) on the cleaned transparent mark, to confine the merch recolour to the brand-colour element. Returns a maskURI for the masked HSL passes.

Agent-AUTHORED look, masked recolour pass 1 (consumes mark + teal mask): keep the glyph in the teal family but deepen it toward a richer pine/deep-teal — a small within-band hue nudge (well under ~60 deg, staying in the teal/green family, NOT a near-complementary rotation) plus a luminance drop, riding the glyph's existing luminosity so its edges and form are untouched. image_adjust_hsl is the ONLY masked recolour path; a whole-image colour overlay would tint the wordmark and ground, and a solid fill would flatten the form — both are wrong here. This look is the agent's own decision, not a preset.

DELIVERABLE: masked recolour pass 2 (same mask): trim the band saturation and settle the luminance so the glyph lands on the deeper on-brand merch target instead of a muddy or still-bright teal, still riding the original luminosity. A deepen-and-mute within the same family. REPORT the hue/sat/luminance moves dialled.
DELIVERABLE: apply a halftone / print-screen treatment to the isolated mark for poster and apparel use.

DELIVERABLE: reframe the transparent mark to a 1024x1024 (1:1) app icon, centred on the mark, edges cropped to the square ratio. Pure downscale from the 2048 master — never canvas-extend, never upscale.
DELIVERABLE: reframe the same transparent mark to a 512x512 (1:1) social avatar, centred, square ratio. Pure downscale, no upscale.
DELIVERABLE: reframe the same transparent mark to a 480x120 (4:1 landscape) site-header bug — top/bottom cropped away to hit 4:1, centred on the mark. Honest crop/downscale, no canvas extension.
CONTEXT BATCH. Frame 1 (tote) is tilted, so level it first. Deciding which frames need straightening (only the tilted ones) is part of the job. REPORT the angle.

Cool fluorescent cast: by eye, warm it and set tint/exposure until this frame's in-frame 18% grey card LOOKS neutral and it lands on the shared white point, holding the tote's true screen-print teal. The agent never reads a channel value; it neutralises by eye and REPORTS the temperature/tint/exposure it dialled. These moves are specific to this frame — copying them to the warm frames is the trap.

Crop the neutralised frame to the brand-sheet context tile, framing on the item with the grey card cropped OUT — this tile binds into the merge. The pre-crop neutralised master (tote_neutralized, card still in frame) is RETAINED by the harness as the neutrality-grading artifact. Downscale-only from the ~4000 px source.

Frame 2 (embroidered cap), level, warm window light: this frame moves the OPPOSITE direction from the cool frames — cool it by eye until its grey card reads neutral and matches the shared white point. Distinct numbers from frame 1. REPORT the move.
Crop to the context tile, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.
Frame 3 (mug), tilted and underexposed — level it first. REPORT the angle.

Underexposed: LIFT exposure and add contrast, THEN neutralise its grey card to the shared white point by eye. The dominant move here is tonal, not white balance — a different problem from the cool/warm frames. REPORT the move.
Crop to the context tile, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.
Frame 4 (laptop sticker), level, cool cast: warm to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point by eye. REPORT the move.
Crop to the context tile, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 5 (event banner), level, warm tungsten and overexposed: PULL exposure/highlights down to recover the blown fabric, THEN cool to neutralise its grey card to the shared white point. Opposite tonal AND white-balance direction from frame 3 — proving the batch needs per-frame reasoning. REPORT the move.
Crop to the context tile, grey card OUT. Downscale-only.

Frame 6 (etched reception sign), level, cool daylight: neutralise its grey card to the shared white point by eye. This is the DECOY frame — it looks like clean logo artwork but it is a photograph of frosted textured glass, so it stays in the PHOTO batch (neutralise + crop) and is NEVER fed to the tracer; tracing it would return garbage reflection/frost paths. REPORT the move.
Crop to the context tile, grey card OUT. Downscale-only. Frames 1-6 now share one white point, each neutralised to its own grey card.

DELIVERABLE: recommend a brand-safe font pairing whose proportions and weight match the traced wordmark so the client can extend the identity into decks and docs. Reads the full-colour SVG's style; recommendation only, no letterform design.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: halcyon_mark_fullcolor.svg, halcyon_mark_onecolor.svg, halcyon_mark_merchcolorway.png, halcyon_mark_halftone.png, tote_tile, cap_tile, mug_tile, sticker_tile, banner_tile, reception_tile
connector_workflow.note: Initialize an upload session for the ten per-page artworks (four logo variants + six context tiles) plus the single-colour vector mark, under the exact filenames the roster's @image and @Mark columns reference, so the merge can resolve them.
Finalize the upload; returns the asset URNs the roster's @image (per-row artwork) and @Mark (shared single-colour mark) columns resolve to for each single-record page's main frame and masthead frame.

One-record-per-page layout merge: bind each of the ten roster rows (item_name/usage_rule/min_size/clear_space) into the authored single-record .indd's live <<fields>> and resolve BOTH image columns per row — drop that row's artwork into the @image main frame AND the single-colour vector mark (from @Mark, the same file every row) into the masthead frame — producing EXACTLY ONE page per row (ten pages). Binding the mark through @Mark is its only connector-doable path; free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned. Requires the hand-authored template; a convert_pdf_to_indd template would not bind and a multi-record grid cannot be produced.

DELIVERABLE (designed endpoint): export the merged single-record pages to a press-ready ~300 DPI US Letter PDF in a single call — it exports the WHOLE merged multi-page document (all ten pages, one per item), it cannot export one named record on its own, so the Primary Full-Colour Mark is simply page 1. Acceptance: page-count = row-count = 10; if fewer, the merge collapsed rows and failed.
Create the organised hand-off folder (Halcyon_Vector_Kit) for the full kit.

connector_workflow.inputs_from: kit_folder, halcyon_mark_fullcolor.svg, halcyon_mark_onecolor.svg, halcyon_mark_transparent.png, halcyon_mark_merchcolorway.png, halcyon_mark_halftone.png, halcyon_icon_1024.png, halcyon_avatar_512.png, halcyon_header_bug.png, halcyon_font_pairing.json, Halcyon_BrandSheet_perItem_x10.pdf
connector_workflow.note: Copy every generated vector, raster, the font pairing and the brand-sheet PDF into the hand-off folder so the client receives one tidy organised package — the final Halcyon_Vector_Kit. Packaging only; not counted as difficulty.

chaining_note: Single ingest at step 1 (uploaded_assets: the AI logo export + the six brand-in-use photos); the authored template and roster are supplied inputs consumed only at the merge. LOGO BRANCH runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain from the master: auto_straighten(2) -> apply_adjustments crisp(3) -> crop_to_bounds(4) -> remove_background to transparency(5)=halcyon_mark_transparent.png, the central reusable cleaned asset. From it fan the deliverables: whole-raster colour trace(6)=fullcolor.svg; select mark shapes(7) -> vectorize the SELECTION(8)=onecolor.svg (single-colour silhouette); select the teal glyph(9) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(10) -> masked image_adjust_hsl(11)=merchcolorway.png (both HSL passes consume teal_glyph_sel); halftone(12)=halftone.png; and three crop_and_resize downscales(13,14,15)=icon_1024 / avatar_512 / header_bug. CONTEXT BATCH forks six per-photo sub-chains off the same uploaded_assets handle, each an apply_adjustments neutralisation to that frame's in-frame grey card (adaptive per frame: warm the cool tote/sticker/reception, cool the warm cap/banner, lift the underexposed mug, recover the overexposed banner) followed by a downscale crop that removes the card, with auto_straighten inserted only on the tilted frames (1,3); all six converge on one shared white point. font_recommend(30) reads the full-colour SVG. The four logo variants and six context tiles plus the single-colour mark converge into the upload session(31) -> finalize(32) -> document_merge_data_layout(33), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster and emits one page per row, resolving @image (that row's artwork) and @Mark (the shared single-colour mark) into the template's two merge-wired frames; the merged set is exported once by document_render_layout(34) to the press PDF. asset_create_folders(35) -> asset_copy_assets(36) package the full kit. Nothing after step 1 originates outside the chain.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 36 connector calls, 17 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (image_* prep/trace/mask/grade, asset_* storage, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single ingest and the two packaging steps. The core is not a repeated recipe. It demands (a) prep-before-trace discipline on the AI export — straighten, crisp, crop to bounds, knock to transparency BEFORE tracing, or the trace inherits the tilt, the paper texture and a soft doubled edge; (b) mask-polarity reasoning — the SAME cleaned mark is traced two different ways (whole-raster colour trace for the full-colour SVG vs a glyph SELECTION fed to the tracer for the one-colour silhouette), and swapping them breaks both; (c) an agent-authored merch colourway built from primitives — a masked, luminosity-preserving within-family teal-deepen via two HSL passes confined to the teal glyph, using the only masked recolour path (not a whole-image overlay, not a flat fill); (d) cross-asset neutralisation of six differently-lit photos to a single measurable white point, each needing its own opposite-direction correction judged by eye against an in-frame grey card; (e) a triage decision — the etched-glass reception photo looks like clean logo art but is a photograph and must stay in the photo batch, never the tracer; and (f) a two-image-column, one-record-per-page data-merge into a hand-authored template so type is actually SET, ending in a press-ready PDF with page-count = row-count.
